solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The greatest space movie!

parts.note: a cryptic tribute to Ridley Scott's 1979 science-fiction horror film, often hailed as the finest film set in outer space

explanation.surface: A film fan's breathless claim about the best ever science-fiction picture.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no wordplay: the whole clue simply points at a celebrated film set aboard a spaceship.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridley Scott's film about a creature stalking a spaceship crew is a contender for the finest film set among the stars.

clue.text: My new wife advanced ££ here to see Jamaica Inn

parts.note: 'Cor!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
each pound sign stands for L, from the Latin libra, so two of them give two Ls

explanation.surface: Someone's new wife lends money to visit a famous inn.
explanation.walkthrough: Jamaica Inn is a real coaching inn on Bodmin Moor in the south-west English county, made famous by Daphne du Maurier's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica Inn stands on Bodmin Moor, so the county containing it is where a visitor goes to see the inn.

clue.text: Old musician into Bach and Elgar

indicators.note: the composer's name is tucked into the words that follow, running across Bach and Elgar

explanation.surface: A list of great composers, with one more said to be among Bach and Elgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals letters concealed within 'Bach and Elgar'; the surface invites you to think of a composer being a fan of the two named.
explanation.definitionFit: The baroque composer of Messiah died in 1759, so he is certainly an old musician.

clue.text: Flipping Shakespeare's monotonous

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round, so the word for Shakespeare is written backwards

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard of Avon

explanation.surface: A mild British curse at how dull Shakespeare is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive but tells you to turn BARD around; the 's is 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and colourless, lacking variety or interest, is a synonym for monotonous.

clue.text: Fish slice skinned, flavoured with this?

definitions.text: Fish slice skinned, flavoured with this?

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

indicators.note: skinning removes the outside, so the word slice loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cook asks what flavouring went with a skinned slice of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinned' strips the outer letters of 'slice' to leave LIC. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a bulb you might well season fish with.
explanation.definitionFit: The pungent bulb is a classic flavouring for fish dishes, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: A riot gun prepared to crush onset of clan battle

indicators.note: the rearranged letters squeeze around the single letter, holding it inside
the letters of a riot gun are made ready in a new arrangement
the onset is the start, so just the first letter of clan

explanation.surface: Riot police ready their weapon to suppress a clan uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges A RIOT GUN to AGINOURT, and 'to crush' puts C, from 'onset of clan', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V's 1415 victory over the French is one of the most famous battles of the Hundred Years' War.

clue.text: Lo, a carpet's unrolled to reveal her

definitions.text: Lo, a carpet's unrolled to reveal her

indicators.note: a rolled-up carpet opened out has its letters spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A rug is opened and, behold, a woman appears from inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unrolled' rearranges LO A CARPET. Plutarch tells how the Egyptian queen was smuggled to Julius Caesar rolled in a carpet, so the whole clue tells her story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen famously had herself delivered to Caesar wrapped in a rug, revealed when it was opened.

clue.text: Freight firm guards silver crossing river

indicators.note: the abbreviation for a firm stands either side of the rest, guarding it

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: the river letter goes through the middle of the symbol for silver

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A shipping company protects a consignment of silver as it crosses a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' and 'crossing' look like a security escort's actions but both signal one piece going inside another, nested two deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by a ship, plane or lorry are its load, a synonym for freight.

clue.text: Formula One's leader evacuated after crashing, getting large blood transfusion!

indicators.note: a car that has crashed is wrecked, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
the opening letter of One is cleared out of the word Formula
the leader is the front, so only the first letter of One's

explanation.surface: A Formula One driver needs a big transfusion after an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's leader' is O, 'evacuated' removes it from FORMULA to leave FRMULA, and 'after crashing' rearranges those letters. The definition is playful: a large amount of blood held in the arms.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount one can carry in the arms is a large quantity, and blood given into an arm makes this a jokey description.

clue.text: I will leave lesson for noon aperitif

indicators.note: the letter I is to depart from the word for lesson
for means in exchange, so the noon letter takes its place

parts.note: a school lesson is a period on the timetable
N is short for noon, as on a clock face

explanation.surface: Someone skips a lesson to have a drink before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I will leave ... for noon' swaps the I in PERIOD for N.
explanation.definitionFit: The French anise-flavoured spirit is traditionally drunk before a meal, as a pre-dinner drink.

clue.text: Return to polish fancy jewellery, making an odd noise

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for polish is written backwards

parts.note: to rub is to polish
bling is slang for flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to cleaning showy jewellery and makes a strange sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' reverses RUB to BUR, which is then followed by BLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a continuous murmuring or bubbling sound, like a stream or a rambling talker, is an odd noise.

clue.text: Punch or ale?

definitions.meaning: British slang for beer or bitter

explanation.surface: A choice of drinks: punch or beer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like the drink but means a blow; the question mark flags the slang sense of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a hard blow and colloquial British slang for beer.

clue.text: Specimen old German coin Joey collected

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the coin gathers the young kangaroo up between its letters

parts.note: PF is short for pfennig, a former German coin
a joey is a young kangaroo, so roo

explanation.surface: A collector picks up a sample of an old German coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joey' is the Australian word for a young kangaroo, and the pfennig was Germany's small coin before the euro; 'collected' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial print or test copy of a book or coin is a specimen of the finished thing.

clue.text: Steal kiss from talent show agent

indicators.note: stealing something takes it away, so the kiss letter goes
from shows which word the letter is taken out of

parts.note: The X Factor is a British TV talent show
X is the symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: An agent snatches a kiss from someone on a talent show.
explanation.walkthrough: The X Factor is a British TV singing contest; 'Steal kiss from' takes away its X.
explanation.definitionFit: In business an agent who buys and sells on another's behalf is a factor, and an agent of change is one too.

clue.text: Islands madcap, ever-decreasing circles

indicators.note: the words madcap and ever-decreasing circle round the name, holding it within them

explanation.surface: A description of a crazy spiralling motion: ever-decreasing circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circles' is a verb: the phrase surrounds the answer. 'Ever-decreasing circles' is also the title of a BBC sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic archipelago off West Africa is a nation made up of islands.

clue.text: Blubbery-sounding character to blub

indicators.note: a character, here a word, that sounds like the blubbery creature when said aloud

parts.note: the blubbery creature of the sea is the whale, thick with fat

explanation.surface: A fat character in a story bursts into tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubbery' points to the whale, and '-sounding character' asks for a word that is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: To blub is to cry noisily, and the howling cry of grief is the same idea.

clue.text: Slobber over visiting retired peer

indicators.note: the over letter calls in, going inside the reversed peer
retired means withdrawn backwards, so the word for peer is reversed

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone fawns over a retired peer on a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses LORD to DROL, and 'visiting' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To let saliva run from the mouth is to slobber, as a dog does at food.

clue.text: Passing medium-dry champagne — not cold

indicators.note: not means without, so the cold letter is dropped

parts.note: demi-sec is the term for a medium-dry champagne
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone passes on medium-dry champagne because it is not chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like a verb about declining the drink but means death; 'not cold' removes C from DEMI-SEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Death is euphemistically called passing, and the formal word for it is a synonym.

clue.text: Roadside check reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the word for check is said and its sound-alike entered

parts.note: to curb is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A report on an inspection of the side of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' gives the sound-alike of CURB, which is also the American spelling of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The stone edging between pavement and road runs along the roadside.

clue.text: Regal kind with daughter getting bumped off?

definitions.text: Regal kind with daughter getting bumped off?

indicators.note: the letters are knocked about into a new order
the daughter letter comes off the word kind

explanation.surface: A royal sort of person whose daughter is murdered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with daughter ... off' drops D from KIND to leave KIN, and 'bumped' rearranges REGAL plus KIN. The whole clue describes Shakespeare's tragic monarch, whose daughter Cordelia is hanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic monarch loses his youngest daughter Cordelia to murder, so a regal figure whose daughter is killed describes him.

clue.text: British news boss, liberal alpha male, creates uproar

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper
alpha is the NATO alphabet word for A

explanation.surface: A British newspaper editor who acts as a liberal alpha male causes a furore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alpha male' looks like one phrase but splits into A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of London's old Bethlem asylum came to mean chaos and wild confusion.

clue.text: Pulse fast … one-fifty!

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A racing pulse, beating fast, at one hundred and fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat but is a seed; 'one-fifty' is Roman I and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the edible seeds of legumes, and the small lens-shaped seed is one of them.

clue.text: Show off apartment crammed with unlimited junk

indicators.note: the apartment word is stuffed with the remaining letters

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: without its limits, junk loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a flat stuffed with endless junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips the ends from 'junk', and 'crammed with' signals that the apartment word holds what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade or display something ostentatiously is to show it off.

clue.text: Mature gagging order in matters for discussion

parts.note: to age is to mature
an NDA, a non-disclosure agreement, is a contract that gags someone

explanation.surface: A mature gagging order is among the issues up for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gagging order' looks like a court injunction but stands for NDA, the initials of a non-disclosure agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be discussed at a meeting is its programme of business.

clue.text: One losing partner making vow in a couple of weeks

indicators.note: the vow sits inside the two week letters

parts.note: W is short for week, so two weeks gives two Ws
'I do' is the vow made at a wedding

explanation.surface: A marriage made in two weeks, with one partner then lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The wedding vow 'I do' goes between W and W; the surface hints at a whirlwind marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose husband has died has lost her partner.

clue.text: Poet's moving sonnet that is entertaining only occasionally

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the rearranged letters take in the others
moving the letters of sonnet about puts them in a new order
occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of only

explanation.surface: A poet's touching sonnet is only sometimes amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges 'sonnet' to TENSON; 'entertaining' takes in the alternate letters picked by 'occasionally'. 'that is' is a link here, not the usual IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was Queen Victoria's Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Flower sent from Victoria to Alexandria?

definitions.text: Flower sent from Victoria to Alexandria?

parts.words: Flower sent from Victoria to Alexandria?
parts.note: a flower here is a thing that flows: the river runs from Lake Victoria to the Mediterranean near the Egyptian port of Alexandria

explanation.surface: A bouquet sent from London's Victoria to someone in Alexandria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means something that flows, a river; the surface suggests a bouquet and London's Victoria station.
explanation.definitionFit: The great African river rises at Lake Victoria and reaches the sea near Alexandria.

clue.text: Dainty city hideaway

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
a lair is an animal's hideaway

explanation.surface: A dainty little city retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dainty' is a noun here: an old word for a delicacy, such as a cream-filled pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dainty is a delicacy, and the cream-filled choux pastry is such a treat.

clue.text: Brief office affairs?

parts.note: the short form of the word for the running of office business, with a hint at brief romances at work

explanation.surface: A question about short-lived flings at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' says the word is clipped, and 'office affairs' means paperwork rather than romance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the clipped form of administration, the routine business of running an office.

clue.text: Film naked Spanish gentleman going round a rocky hill

indicators.note: going round means turning back, so the stripped word is reversed
naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go

parts.note: a hidalgo is a Spanish nobleman or gentleman
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A naked Spanish gentleman walks around a rocky hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips the outer letters, leaving IDALG, and 'going round' turns that back; tors are the rocky outcrops of English moorland such as Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridley Scott's 2000 epic about a Roman arena fighter won the Oscar for Best Picture.
